items.claim: The seam after 14:5 holds, but the stated reason for rejecting 14:1-14:12 as one unit does not discriminate. The row says the thesis closes at 14:5 on the building-up purpose clause, yet 14:12 restates both that building-up purpose and the zeal-for-spiritual-things exhortation of 14:1. On the row's own criterion, that return favours a close at 14:12. The rejection must rest on the new argument opened at 14:6 (a hypothetical visit with a fresh vocative), which the row mentions only as a second reason, and the 14:12 echo is left unweighed.
items.both_sides: For the row: 14:5 does end on a purpose clause and 14:6 opens a new hypothetical argument with an adversative adverb and vocative, so the seam and medium confidence stand. Against the wording: the building-up and zeal vocabulary of 14:1 and 14:5 returns at 14:12, an echo that on the stated criterion supports the rival 14:1-14:12 unit; the rival is answered only by the 14:6 onset, not by the 14:5 close.

suggested_fix.fact: 14:12 repeats the building-up purpose of 14:5 and the zeal for spirits of 14:1; this echo closes the analogy run of 14:6-14:12 rather than the thesis, and the rival is rejected because 14:6 opens a new argument.

items.claim: The rationale says the repetition of the application formula frames the analogies, but the two occurrences are parallel applications, not a frame. The formula at 14:9 applies the instrument analogies of 14:7-14:8, and the same formula at 14:12 applies the speech analogy of 14:10-14:11. Because 14:9 stands inside the analogy run, the repetition cannot bracket 14:7-14:11; it is a twice-applied refrain whose second occurrence closes the unit. The seam after 14:12 and medium_low confidence stand.
items.both_sides: For the row: the formula does recur and its second occurrence does fall in the closing verse, so it supports the close at 14:12. Against the wording: a frame stands before and after the framed material, while 14:9 stands between the two analogy pairs; calling it a frame misdescribes the device that the close relies on.

suggested_fix.fact: The application formula recurs at 14:9 and 14:12, each time applying one analogy pair to the hearers; the second application closes the unit.

items.claim: The divided-reading sentence states that 14:34-14:35 stands in divided readings in debates over ordination without a tier label. The strategy's only source for that context is REPORTED (hardness_batch_03). The sentence also does not name the readings or their holders, which strategy §7B and the §8 close check (item 9) require. Secondary finding: the closing claim that both wordings are given wherever the two editions differ in 14:34-14:35 overclaims. At least two RP/SBL differences without an SBL critical sign are not given: the noun at 14:35 (RP plural, SBL singular) and the adversative at 14:34 (RP elided, SBL full). The seam, the INFERRED backward attachment of 14:36 and low confidence stand.
items.both_sides: For the row: it prefers no reading, keeps the debate out of the seam reasoning, labels the transposition REPORTED, and discloses every SBL-signed site in 14:34-14:35. Against: an unlabelled report reads as an assertion (OW-18 provenance tiers), the strategy requires readings and holders to be named, and 'both wordings are given' is a universal claim that the unsigned differences falsify. The pinned inputs do not name the readings or their holders, so the minimum available fix is the REPORTED label with its source, plus narrowing the both-wordings claim to the signed sites.
